title: Perceptron in Machine Learning | Explained with a Cricket Match #shorts #ai #tech
text:
Perceptron in machine learning, explained with one simple question: should I go to the Sunday cricket match?

A perceptron gives every input a weight (how important it is), adds everything up, and says yes only if the total is above a limit. We work through a small example: weights five, three and minus six, limit four, total two, so the answer is no. We also see that real perceptrons learn their weights from examples, that the idea is from about 1958 (Frank Rosenblatt), and that one perceptron makes one straight split.

Sources: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1706.04946, https://scikit-learn.org/1.1/modules/generated/sklearn.linear_model.Perceptron.html, https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/760225-first-artificial-neural-network

title: AI vs Machine Learning vs Deep Learning vs Generative AI
text:
AI vs machine learning vs deep learning vs generative AI: not the same thing. Here's the one picture that fits them.
🧠 Artificial intelligence: the big circle. Machines doing tasks that need intelligence, even a chess program built from hand-written rules.
📈 Machine learning: inside AI. It learns from examples instead of rules, like a spam filter trained on millions of emails.
🕸️ Deep learning: inside machine learning. Many-layered neural networks, behind face unlock and speech recognition.
✨ Generative AI: inside deep learning. It creates new text, images and code, like ChatGPT.
So ChatGPT is generative AI, which is deep learning, which is machine learning, which is AI.
